tasks.title: HANGS Construction Services · FY2026 Payroll Audit
tasks.description: Audit HANGS Construction Services LLC's FY2026 payroll from 7 Excel, PDF and Word files: the trial balance and payroll expense ledger, the payroll register with every paycheck and the employee master, the HR log of rate changes and leavers, the support for the audit team's sample, the four Form 941 summaries and the controller's written answers. Analytics by month and headcount, ghost-employee tests on the whole master file, a stratified sample traced to timesheets, rate approvals and personnel files with gross to net recomputed, every rate change and leaver tested, and the register tied to the ledger, the June 30 accrual and the Forms 941. Produce formula-linked workpapers with tickmarks and a draft findings memo. The CPA reviews, decides every open item and concludes; the machine gives no opinion.

light.reason: Waiting for review: draft package ready, open items remain

tasks.outputs: Two files: formula-linked Excel workpapers with tickmarks and evidence tabs, and a draft payroll findings memo PDF for the CPA with evidence trails and the original files attached

tasks.gates: Draft workpapers and findings, not reviewed, concluded or signed. Not an audit report and no opinion. Open items stay open. The CPA concludes.

propertyEvents.result: Run the ghost-employee tests on the whole master file and every paycheck
propertyEvents.locator: Register by Payday!A8:AB37, Paychecks!A8:G2501 and Employee Master!A8:O107

propertyEvents.result: Of the five tests, one flag: Xavier Baptiste (E-1044) and Alicia Baptiste (E-1051) are paid into the same account ending 7330 (GHOST-01). No two people share a Social Security number, every paycheck is to someone in the master, and everyone in the master was paid. A shared account is how a fictitious employee’s pay reaches a real one, so it is put to the controller and the personnel files in stage 4.

Reading FY2026 payroll sample support.pdf

propertyEvents.result: Draw the stratified sample with the plan’s seed and trace each paycheck to its timesheet, rate approval and personnel file
propertyEvents.locator: PDF pages 1-10; earnings statement, timesheet, rate authorization and personnel file for each sampled paycheck, then the shared account and the rate change forms

propertyEvents.result: 8 paychecks drawn: S-1 Quentin Ferreira (PR-25-19), S-2 Mei Oyelaran (PR-26-02), S-3 Rafael Thorvaldsen (PR-26-02), S-4 Talia Quintero (PR-25-17) and 4 more, $35,828.19 of gross pay. Each agrees from the register to the earnings statement: hours to an approved timesheet or the salaried attendance confirmation, the rate to an approved personnel action form and the master file, and the I-9, W-4, deferral elections and deposit form to the personnel file.
propertyEvents.locator: PDF pages 1-10; earnings statement, timesheet, rate authorization and personnel file for each sampled paycheck, then the shared account and the rate change forms

propertyEvents.result: Recompute gross pay, every withholding and net pay on each sampled paycheck
propertyEvents.locator: PDF pages 1-10; earnings statement, timesheet, rate authorization and personnel file for each sampled paycheck, then the shared account and the rate change forms

propertyEvents.result: Gross pay, the 401(k) deferral, the Section 125 premium, Social Security (to each year’s wage base), Medicare, Paid Leave and WA Cares recompute to the cent on all 8; income tax withheld is the payroll system’s from each W-4 and agrees to the register. The L&I employee share does not: on the 3 craft paychecks with overtime payroll took it on time and a half, $4.94 too much in the sample (WH-01, Q7). L&I counts an overtime hour as one hour. Across the year’s 8,570 overtime hours that is roughly $2,514.64 owed back to the crews.
propertyEvents.locator: PDF pages 1-10; earnings statement, timesheet, rate authorization and personnel file for each sampled paycheck, then the shared account and the rate change forms

propertyEvents.result: 8 paychecks traced and recomputed · $4.94 of L&I over-deducted on overtime (WH-01)
Rate Changes and Leavers
Reading FY2026 rate changes and terminations.xlsx
propertyEvents.locator: Rate Changes!A8:K12 and Terminations!A8:H13; every FY2026 rate change and leaver

propertyEvents.result: Read FY2026 rate changes and terminations.xlsx: 5 rate changes and 6 leavers.

propertyEvents.result: Find every pay rate change in the paychecks and vouch each one to an approved personnel action form
propertyEvents.locator: Rate Changes!A8:K12 and Terminations!A8:H13; every FY2026 rate change and leaver

propertyEvents.result: The paychecks show 5 rate changes, all effective December 22, 2025, and the HR log has the same 5. Four have a personnel action form signed by the Chief Financial Officer or the President and CEO before payroll entered them. The fifth is Renata Salazar’s own salary, $88,000.00 to $98,000.00: she entered it herself and the form is not signed (RATE-01). Q4 says it was agreed in her review; nothing on file shows it. It added $4,999.93 to her pay in 13 paychecks to June 30.
propertyEvents.locator: Rate Changes!A8:K12 and Terminations!A8:H13; every FY2026 rate change and leaver

propertyEvents.result: Test that every leaver was paid a final check and nothing after it, and that nobody is paid who should have left
propertyEvents.locator: Rate Changes!A8:K12 and Terminations!A8:H13; every FY2026 rate change and leaver

propertyEvents.result: 6 people left in FY2026. Each was paid one final check, on the payday for the period with the last day worked, and payroll inactivated them that day: Corbin Ashgrove (October 10, last paid October 17), Renzo Valloton (December 5, last paid December 12), Zoe Xiong (February 13, last paid February 20) and the others. Nobody was paid after a final check, and everyone still in the master was paid on the last payday, June 26, 2026 (Q5).
propertyEvents.locator: Rate Changes!A8:K12 and Terminations!A8:H13; every FY2026 rate change and leaver

propertyEvents.result: Put the shared deposit account to the controller and check the answer against the personnel files
propertyEvents.locator: Word document; eight payroll questions and the controller’s written answers of September 18, 2026

propertyEvents.result: Q3: Xavier Baptiste and Alicia Baptiste are married and asked to be paid into their joint account. The personnel files agree: both deposit forms name the joint account and both holders, each has an I-9 and a W-4, they were hired on different dates (November 11, 2018 and December 15, 2022) and their hours are approved by different superintendents. Both worked every payday. The red flag is cleared (GHOST-01); the CPA reviews the clearance.
propertyEvents.locator: Word document; eight payroll questions and the controller’s written answers of September 18, 2026

propertyEvents.result: 5 rate changes, one unapproved (RATE-01) · 6 leavers removed on time · the shared account cleared by inquiry (GHOST-01)

Reading FY2026 Form 941 filing summaries.pdf
propertyEvents.locator: PDF pages 1-4; one Form 941 filing summary per quarter, lines 1 to 14

propertyEvents.result: Read FY2026 Form 941 filing summaries.pdf: four quarterly summaries, July 2025 to June 2026, lines 1 to 14.
propertyEvents.locator: PDF pages 1-4; one Form 941 filing summary per quarter, lines 1 to 14

propertyEvents.result: Tie the register to the ledger’s wages, with the accrual reversed in July and the accrual booked at June 30
propertyEvents.locator: Register by Payday!A8:AB37, Paychecks!A8:G2501 and Employee Master!A8:O107

propertyEvents.result: Field wages paid $9,102,218.35, less the June 30, 2025 accrual reversed on July 1 ($209,221.42), plus the June 30, 2026 accrual ($237,074.66), is the ledger’s $9,130,071.59 to the cent; office salaries the same way, $2,927,123.19. Employer Social Security and Medicare $880,857.32 is the register’s, payroll by payroll.
propertyEvents.locator: Register by Payday!A8:AB37, Paychecks!A8:G2501 and Employee Master!A8:O107

propertyEvents.result: Recompute the June 30 accrued wages from the July 10 payroll, and the employer taxes on them
propertyEvents.locator: Register by Payday!A8:AB37, Paychecks!A8:G2501 and Employee Master!A8:O107

propertyEvents.result: The July 10 payroll paid $419,830.58 for June 22 to July 5: seven of its nine working days for hourly crews and seven of ten for salaried staff were June’s, $314,193.66, against the $314,193.69 accrued (($0.03), rounding on each paycheck). The wages are cut off correctly. Their employer Social Security and Medicare, $22,864.35 at that payroll’s own rate, is not: it was expensed in July and nothing is accrued, as Q6 says (ACC-01). The same was true a year earlier ($19,972.25), so FY2026 expense is short $2,892.10 and the June 30 liability $22,864.35.
propertyEvents.locator: Register by Payday!A8:AB37, Paychecks!A8:G2501 and Employee Master!A8:O107

tape.label: Employer Taxes on the Accrual, Not Accrued

propertyEvents.result: Agree each quarter of the register to its Form 941 as filed
propertyEvents.locator: PDF pages 1-4; one Form 941 filing summary per quarter, lines 1 to 14

propertyEvents.result: Each quarter’s register agrees to its Form 941 as filed: wages on line 2 ($11,369,726.27 for the year), income tax withheld, Social Security and Medicare wages, and the employees on the pay period including the 12th. Line 12 differs from the register’s taxes only by cents, the employer’s share rounded on each payroll against the quarter. All four were filed on time. Q2 2026 includes the June 26 bonus run.
propertyEvents.locator: PDF pages 1-4; one Form 941 filing summary per quarter, lines 1 to 14

propertyEvents.result: The register ties to the ledger and all four 941s · wages cut off correctly · $22,864 of employer taxes not accrued (ACC-01)
Ready for the CPA
Add up what was found and set it against materiality

Known misstatement: FY2026 expense short $2,892.10 and the June 30 liability $22,864.35 (ACC-01), with roughly $2,514.64 owed back to the crews for the L&I over-deduction (WH-01): $25,378.99 of liabilities, 7.5% of the $340,000.00 materiality. The rest is control: Renata Salazar raised her own pay without a signed approval ($4,999.93 paid, RATE-01). The ghost-employee flag is cleared (GHOST-01). Concluding is the CPA’s job; the machine stops here.
